A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BigDocs research and contain complete, readable main text and appendices. Tables, figures, formal definitions, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations in Tables 2 and 3, human evaluations in Section 5.3, contamination measurements, and appendix ablation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original model evaluations, human-study results, contamination measurements, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The data-curation pipeline, toolkit, continual pretraining, and downstream finetuning remain unchanged. Sections 3–5 and Appendix A.5 introduce no revised architecture, objective, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BigDocs data sources, ten BigDocs-Bench tasks, general document benchmarks, and appendix analysis coverage. GUI task-name edits refer to existing tasks.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 2, 3, and 8 are unchanged. Table 2 newly qualifies instruction-tuned rows as reference-only comparisons, but retains the same evaluated methods and scores.

E3.justification: Splits, training budgets, model configurations, preprocessing, and metrics remain unchanged. Human evaluation still uses 28 evaluators and 1,900 annotations; revised outcome descriptions clarify choices already represented in v1's Figures 5 and 12.

E4.justification: The contamination analysis, data-curation and context-length ablations, benchmark correlations, and qualitative success/failure cases are retained. Appendix A.12, Table 29, and Figures 18–22 already contain these supplementary analyses in v1.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged, including Table 1's token-length means and standard deviations and the human-verification reporting. No repeated-run information, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including appendix results. Phi3.5-Vision + BigDocs retains averages of 60.80 in Table 2 and 56.34 in Table 3. Figure 5 labels existing preference proportions without changing the outcomes.

T1.justification: Formal task formulations in Appendix A.4 and metric definitions in Appendix A.6 remain unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The dataset, benchmark, toolkit, model contributions, and principal performance claims remain the same. Although the title drops 'permissively-licensed,' the abstract and conclusion retain the licensing claim, so its scientific scope is not narrowed.

C2.justification: Table 2 now explicitly describes instruction-tuned results as 'provided for reference only (unfair comparison),' adding a qualification absent from v1's caption. Existing mechanism explanations, failure analyses, and stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The introduction changes from promising open-sourcing upon acceptance to stating that datasets, models, and documentation are open-sourced. Implementation details and access links remain unchanged. The conclusion and reproducibility statement still describe release in future tense, leaving the precise availability status unclear.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior datasets and multimodal models remain unchanged. The small wording edits do not revise novelty claims or the relationship to earlier research.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, updates the publication header and acknowledgments, standardizes some GUI terminology, and clarifies human-evaluation wording. The section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn with explicit percentages and outcome labels. Table 2 visually distinguishes instruction-tuned rows, and Table 3 restyles group headings. Figure 2 and Tables 1, 2, and 8 are relocated, with limited accompanying page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: The new Table 2 qualification helps readers interpret comparisons appropriately, while Figure 5 and Section 5.3 make human-preference outcomes clearer. These are useful, limited improvements; the scientific evidence and appendix analyses remain unchanged. Inconsistent release-status wording prevents treating the open-sourcing statement as a substantial reproducibility gain.
